blocks.content: The Supreme Court is the guarantor of fundamental rights and the guardian of the Constitution.

items: Article 136 (Special Leave Petition) is a discretionary power of the Supreme Court and does not apply to decisions of military tribunals.
The advisory opinion provided by the Supreme Court under Article 143 is not a judicial pronouncement and is not binding on the President.
The Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32 is narrower than a High Court's under Article 226, as Article 32 applies exclusively to Fundamental Rights.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Original jurisdiction under Article 131 exclusively covers federal disputes involving the Centre and States or inter-state conflicts.
Writ jurisdiction under Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari for enforcing Fundamental Rights.
Appellate jurisdiction spans Constitutional (Article 132), Civil (Article 133), Criminal matters (Article 134), and Special Leave Petitions (Article 136).
Under Article 143, the President can seek advisory opinions from the Supreme Court on questions of law or public importance, which are non-binding in nature.
As a Court of Record under Article 129, its judgments have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when produced before any subordinate court.
